title: The last ferry
summary_es: Un relato: Ines lleva tres semanas viajando con una lista de cosas que ver, hasta que una isla sin nada que visitar le cambia el ritmo.
prediction_prompt: Do you plan every day of a trip, or do you prefer to decide as you go?

sentences.text: By the time Ines reached the harbour, the last ferry of the day was already untying its ropes.

She ran the final hundred metres with her rucksack bouncing against her back, waving one arm, and a man in an orange jacket held the gate open with the expression of someone who had seen this many times before.
She had not planned to visit the island at all.
Ines was not the kind of person who changed her plans.
Her itinerary, printed and folded inside her passport, said that she should be in the capital by now, waiting in a queue for a famous museum.
But the night before, in a hostel kitchen, an old woman peeling oranges had told her about a place where there were no cars and the bakery opened only when the baker felt like it.
Ines had laughed.
Then she had lain awake thinking about it.
The crossing took an hour.
She stood at the back and watched the mainland shrink until it was no more than a grey line.
For three weeks she had been ticking things off a list: cathedrals, viewpoints, dishes she was supposed to try.
She had hundreds of photographs and could barely remember taking them.
It occurred to her that she had been travelling the way she worked, efficiently and without looking up.
The island had one street.
It climbed from the harbour past a shop, a church the size of a garage and a café where four men were playing cards as though it were a serious profession.
There was no museum, no monument, nothing that any guidebook would have troubled to mention.
Nobody tried to sell her anything.
A dog followed her for a while and then lost interest.
She found a room above the café.
The owner, a broad woman called Dora, did not ask how long she was staying; she simply pointed at the key and went back to her soup.
That evening Ines sat on the harbour wall with bread, cheese and a tomato that actually tasted of something.
The light went from gold to pink to a blue so deep it seemed to have weight.
She did not take a single photograph.
Had anyone asked her why, she could not have explained.
She meant to stay one night.
On the third morning Dora put a coffee in front of her without being asked, and one of the card players nodded as if she had always been there.
She helped Dora carry boxes from the morning boat, learned the names of two of the card players, and went swimming every afternoon from a rock that nobody else seemed to use.
One evening Ines took out her itinerary, looked at it for a moment, and used it to wipe the table.
On the ferry back, five days later, the man in the orange jacket recognised her.
"You were in a hurry last time," he said.
"Not any more," said Ines, and she chose a seat facing the island, so that she could watch it for as long as it remained in sight.

language_focus.explanation_es: *She had not planned…*, *an old woman had told her…*, *Ines had laughed*: el *past perfect* cuenta lo que pasó antes del momento del relato, sin tener que ordenar los hechos cronológicamente.
*Had anyone asked her why, she could not have explained* = *If anyone had asked her why…* Inversión literaria del tercer condicional.

tasks.prompt: What is the story mainly about?

options.text: A tourist who gets lost on an island
A traveller who learns to slow down
A woman who decides to move abroad for good
A holiday ruined by bad planning

tasks.rationale_es: Ines viajaba como trabajaba, tachando una lista; en la isla aprende a parar.

tasks.prompt: Before the island, how did Ines usually travel?

options.text: By following a strict list of things to see
Slowly, without making any kind of plan in advance
Always with a group
Only to islands

tasks.rationale_es: Llevaba tres semanas tachando catedrales, miradores y platos de una lista.

tasks.prompt: Why did Ines go to the island?

options.text: It was on her itinerary
She missed her train to the capital
A stranger had described it to her
A friend of hers lived there

tasks.rationale_es: Una anciana, en la cocina del albergue, le habló del lugar la noche anterior.

tasks.prompt: What does "Then she had lain awake thinking about it" suggest?

options.text: She was worried about how much it would cost
The idea attracted her more than she admitted
The hostel was noisy
She was angry with the old woman

tasks.rationale_es: Se rio, pero no pudo dormir pensando en ello: la idea la había atrapado.

tasks.prompt: In paragraph 3, "ticking things off a list" means…

options.text: forgetting the things she wanted to see
adding new places to visit
marking each thing as done
writing a diary

tasks.rationale_es: *Tick off* = ir tachando lo que ya está hecho.

tasks.prompt: Ines remembered clearly the moment she took each photograph.
tasks.rationale_es: *She could barely remember taking them*: apenas recordaba haberlas hecho.

options.text: Full of shops for tourists
Large, with several villages
Modern and expensive
Quiet, with almost nothing to visit

tasks.rationale_es: Una sola calle, una tienda, una iglesia diminuta y un café.

tasks.prompt: Why does the writer mention that Ines "did not take a single photograph"?

options.text: She was living the moment instead of collecting it
Her phone had been broken on the ferry crossing
Photography was not allowed
The light was too poor

tasks.rationale_es: Contrasta con los cientos de fotos que no recordaba haber hecho: ahora mira, no colecciona.

tasks.prompt: What does Ines do with her itinerary in paragraph 6?

options.text: She follows it again
She gives it to Dora
She throws it into the sea
She treats it as a cloth

tasks.rationale_es: *She used it to wipe the table*.

options.text: She has stopped caring about her original plan
She is angry with Dora
She has lost her passport
She wants to leave as quickly as she possibly can

tasks.rationale_es: El plan impreso ya solo le sirve de trapo: ha dejado de importarle.

tasks.prompt: Ines stayed on the island for one night, as she had intended.
tasks.rationale_es: Pensaba quedarse una noche y volvió cinco días después.

tasks.prompt: Dora had lived on the island all her life.
tasks.rationale_es: De Dora solo sabemos que lleva el café y alquila la habitación; no se dice de dónde es.

tasks.prompt: Why does the man in the orange jacket appear at both the beginning and the end?

options.text: To show that the ferry is always late
To frame the story and show how Ines has changed
Because he is an old friend of Ines and her family
To explain the timetable

tasks.rationale_es: Abre y cierra el relato: al principio Ines corre; al final, él mismo nota que ya no tiene prisa.
